 **Optional worktree runtime.** `pose runtime start` starts, detached, a runtime for this worktree; `attach` and `status` handshake with it, `stop` drains it (`--drain <d>`, default 5s) and says how many requests in flight finished and how many were abandoned, `restart` is stop then start, and `serve` runs it in the foreground (`--idle <d>`, default 30m, stops an idle runtime; 0 never does). It is opt-in: no other command starts it, and every command runs standalone whether it runs or not. The runtime is identified by the user, the canonical worktree (symlinks resolved) and the Git common directory, so two worktrees of one repository, or two users, never share one; the handshake compares the engine, build, protocol and schema as well and an attach from another engine is refused naming the field. Its endpoint is a Unix domain socket (Linux, macOS) of mode 0600 in a 0700 directory owned by the user (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pose`, else `pose-runtime-<uid>` under the temporary directory, or `POSE_RUNTIME_DIR`), whose peer the operating system identifies before a byte is read; a link, a loose mode, another owner or a file that is not a socket is refused, and a socket nobody answers on is replaced. There is no TCP and no token. Slice 1 hosts no domain operation: it answers handshake, status and stop, confers no authority, signature or presence, and every restart has a new epoch, inheriting nothing. On Windows, which has no named-pipe implementation here, `status` reports `unsupported` and every command runs standalone. `status` exits 0 for running, standalone and unsupported and 1 for an incompatible runtime; `attach` also exits 1 when there is nothing to attach to. `--json` prints the document `pose.runtime.status/1`.

Two medium defects block approval and four low ones are follow-ups. All focused `internal/pose` tests passed, as did `TestReviewRoundsKeepTheCheckoutPathOfTheirThread`.

Several other focused `internal/cli` tests failed here. The failures I inspected report `/home belongs to another user; set XDG_STATE_HOME…`, a sandbox restriction. I did not inspect every failure, and I relied on the sealed `unit:pose-mcp/go/test` instead of running the full suite or `validate`.

`go clean -cache` and the `go-build*` removal both succeeded inside the sandbox, and the checkout was clean just before.

| N3 | low | `review_dispatch.go:2270` | A cancelled wait reports "directory already exists, remove it". Waits reached during replanning ignore cancellation. |
| N4 | low | `review_dispatch.go:774` | After a claim conflict, the replan's specific refusal is dropped and the raw conflict is returned. |
| N5 | low | `POSE.md:956` | The manual does not describe a checkout moved after planning while the session continues, and the spec records no decision for it. |
| N6 | low | `pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_rounds.go:701` | The held path is checked twice, so the recorded reason can end up with an empty path. |

On your three questions:
- **Sharing a directory:** I found no way for a continuation to share one, since creation is exclusive.
- **Hiding a live run's directory:** the fallback does not take or remove it. The resumed session may still refer to the old path, though (N5).
- **Re-running a recorded continuation:** I found no path that re-runs one, but the wrong one can be returned (N1).
